title: Her Own Voice
story_text:
Six weeks later, the garden changed. The town gave the plots to the gardeners themselves. From that spring the community garden was an autonomous project: the gardeners made the rules, kept the money, and chose what to grow. Each plot was independent, but the gardeners met every Saturday to share seeds and tools.

Mr. Bell put a small sign on his fence. It said: ASK ME BEFORE YOU PICK.

Mia's story came out in the school paper with her name under the title. On Monday three teachers stopped her in the hall to say they had read it.

To her surprise, she felt confident at her next interview. She asked better questions, and she listened longer. The confidence did not come from the praise. It came from the two days she spent reading old records until she understood what had happened.

Mr. Bell called her an intelligent young writer, which made her laugh, because she had begun with a rude question.

Her belief in small, careful work had grown into something solid. She kept the four-line note in her notebook, and she kept looking for the next true story.
translation_zh:
六周后，花园变了。镇上把菜地交给了园丁们自己。从那年春天起，社区花园成了一个自治的项目：园丁们自己定规矩、管钱、决定种什么。每块地都是独立的，但园丁们每周六都会聚在一起交换种子和工具。

贝尔先生在他那边的栅栏上挂了块小牌子，上面写着：摘之前先问我。

米娅的报道登在了校报上，标题下面印着她的名字。周一有三个老师在走廊里叫住她，说他们读过了。

让她意外的是，下一次采访时她感到很自信。她问的问题更好了，听的时间也更长了。这份信心并不来自夸奖，而来自她花两天读旧记录、直到弄明白发生了什么的那段日子。

贝尔先生称她是个聪明的年轻作者，这让她笑了，因为她是从一个粗鲁的问题开始的。

她对细小而认真的事情的信念，已经长成了某种结实的东西。她把那张四行笔记留在笔记本里，也继续寻找下一个真实的故事。

title: Alarm, Then Relief
story_text:
The news moved through the town in one afternoon. The school sent home a short, alarming letter. The shop owner put a note in his window, and by evening the whole street was talking about the poisonous plant.

The alarm was real, but it was also louder than the danger. Parents called the garden office all night. One man said he would pull out every plant in the garden himself.

On Wednesday the tests came back. Only one plant was poisonous, and only that one. The other twenty plots were safe.

The relief in the garden was easy to see. People laughed, then went quiet, then laughed again.

But Mia wanted to determine exactly how the plant had arrived. She read old garden records for two days. In the end she found the answer: a seed list from twelve years ago, with one strange name written in the margin.

She was determined to publish it, even if it was only a small fact. She still had faith in small facts. A short true story, she thought, can protect a whole street.
translation_zh:
这个消息一个下午就传遍了小镇。学校发下来一封简短的、令人惊恐的信。店主在橱窗上贴了张纸条，到了晚上，整条街都在谈论那株有毒的植物。

恐慌是真实的，但也比危险本身更响。家长们整夜给花园办公室打电话。有个男人说他要亲自把花园里的植物全拔光。

周三，检测结果出来了。只有一株植物有毒，也只有那一株。另外二十块地都是安全的。

花园里的宽慰显而易见。人们先笑，然后安静下来，然后又笑起来。

但米娅想查明这株植物究竟是怎么来的。她花了两天读花园的旧记录。最后她找到了答案：一份十二年前的种子清单，页边写着一个奇怪的名字。

她决心把它发表出来，哪怕只是一个很小的事实。她依然信任小事实。一个简短的真相，她想，可以保护一整条街。

vocabulary.grammar_note: 不可数名词；常用 a sense of relief（松了一口气）、to my relief（让我宽慰的是）。

vocabulary.story_sentence: The relief in the garden was easy to see.

vocabulary.story_sentence: She was determined to publish it, even if it was only a small fact.

vocabulary.grammar_note: have faith in somebody/something 表示“信任、信赖”；也指宗教信仰。
vocabulary.story_sentence: She still had faith in small facts.

title: The Poisonous Berry
story_text:
On Monday morning Mia went back to the community garden. Mr. Bell was not alone. A small crowd stood around his plot, and his dog, Rusty, lay on the grass and would not stand up.

"The berries," a neighbour said. "He ate the berries."

The vet came quickly. She held up a small red berry and spoke slowly so everyone could hear. "This plant is poisonous. Two more berries could have been fatal for a dog his size."

Mia's stomach turned. There was poison in the middle of the garden, and children played there every day.

"Where did it come from?" she asked.

Mr. Bell pointed at the fence. "The previous owner of this plot liked strange plants. The former gardener grew them for colour, not for food. When I took the plot, I never asked what they were."

Rusty was precious to him. His hands shook as he held the dog's head.

Mia wrote down every word, and this time she was not writing four lines.
translation_zh:
周一早上，米娅回到社区花园。贝尔先生不是一个人。一小群人围在他的菜地边，他的狗拉斯蒂躺在草地上，站不起来。

「是那些浆果，」一个邻居说，「他吃了那些浆果。」

兽医很快就来了。她举起一颗红色的小浆果，说得很慢，让每个人都能听见。「这种植物有毒。再多两颗，对他这个体型的狗来说就可能是致命的。」

米娅的胃里一阵翻腾。花园正中央有毒药，而孩子们每天都在那里玩。

「它是从哪来的？」她问。

贝尔先生指了指栅栏。「这块地上一任主人喜欢奇怪的植物。以前那位园丁种它们是为了颜色，不是为了吃。我接手这块地时，从没问过它们是什么。」

拉斯蒂对他来说是珍宝。他抱着狗的头，双手在发抖。

米娅把每个字都记了下来，这一次她写的不是四行字。
image_prompt: Warm editorial illustration for a 4:3 card: worried neighbours gathered around an old gardener who holds his sick dog on the grass, red berries on a leafy plant beside the fence, late afternoon light, muted warm palette, no text, no watermark.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 作名词指毒药、毒素；作动词指“毒死、毒害”，如 poison the water。
vocabulary.story_sentence: There was poison in the middle of the garden, and children played there every day.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 由 poison + -ous 构成；poisonous 是“本身有毒”，poisoned 是“被下了毒的”。
vocabulary.meaning_zh: 引起中毒的；有毒的；分泌毒素的
vocabulary.story_sentence: This plant is poisonous.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 指造成死亡的；a fatal mistake 也可指“致命的错误”。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Two more berries could have been fatal for a dog his size.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 指珍贵、宝贵；be precious to somebody 表示“对某人来说很珍贵”。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Rusty was precious to him.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 指时间或顺序上的“上一个”，如 the previous week；与 next 相对。
vocabulary.story_sentence: The previous owner of this plot liked strange plants.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 指“以前的、前任的”，只放在名词前；the former 与 the latter 相对。
vocabulary.meaning_zh: 以前的；(两者中) 前者的
vocabulary.story_sentence: The former gardener grew them for colour, not for food.

title: Under Pressure
story_text:
By Friday, Mia was under pressure. The paper went to print on Monday, and she still had no story.

Her editor, Dan, pressed her every morning. "Four lines about a garden is not a story," he said.

The stress made her sleep badly. She drank too much coffee and forgot to eat lunch. The office was small, and the tension between them was easy to feel. Every time Dan looked at her desk, she stared at her screen and typed nothing.

The deadline was tough, but the truth was simple: she did not want to write a safe story about flowers. She wanted to know why Mr. Bell had pulled out every plant in his plot.

On Sunday evening she opened her notebook again. The pressure was still there, but it had changed shape. It no longer felt like a wall in front of her. It felt like a question she had to answer.

She picked up her pen and wrote the first honest line of her story.
translation_zh:
到了周五，米娅感到压力很大。报纸周一就要付印，她还没有故事可写。

她的编辑丹每天早上都催她。「关于花园的四行字不算故事，」他说。

这种压力让她睡不好觉。她喝了太多咖啡，忘了吃午饭。办公室很小，两人之间的紧张关系很容易察觉。每次丹看向她的桌子，她就盯着屏幕，一个字也打不出来。

截稿期限很艰难，但事实很简单：她不想写一篇关于花朵的安全稿子。她想知道贝尔先生为什么把菜地里的植物全拔了。

周日傍晚，她又打开了笔记本。压力还在，但形状变了。它不再像面前的一堵墙，而像一个她必须回答的问题。

她拿起笔，写下了这个故事第一句诚实的话。

vocabulary.grammar_note: 介词短语，常与 be、feel、work 连用，如 work under pressure（在压力下工作）。
vocabulary.story_sentence: By Friday, Mia was under pressure.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 不可数名词，指精神或身体上的压力；动词 stress 表示“强调”。
vocabulary.story_sentence: The stress made her sleep badly.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 本义是“按、压”，也指“催促、敦促”；名词 the press 指新闻界。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Her editor, Dan, pressed her every morning.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 不可数名词；put pressure on somebody 表示“对某人施压”。
vocabulary.story_sentence: The pressure was still there, but it had changed shape.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 口语常用，指“艰难的、棘手的”；形容人时表示“强硬、不好惹”。
vocabulary.story_sentence: The deadline was tough, but the truth was simple: she did not want to write a safe story about flowers.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 指关系或气氛上的紧张，常用 tension between A and B。
vocabulary.story_sentence: The office was small, and the tension between them was easy to feel.

title: The Awkward Question
story_text:
Mia was the newest writer on the school paper, and her first assignment made her anxious. She had to interview Mr. Bell, the old gardener at the community garden. Her hands shook as she opened her notebook.

"Why does your plot look dead?" she asked.

The question was rude, and she knew it at once. Mr. Bell went quiet. The silence between them was awkward, and her face turned red. It was the most embarrassing minute of her week.

But Mr. Bell only smiled. "Because I pulled everything out," he said. "I am curious about what will grow next."

Mia wrote a brief note, thanked him, and walked home through the cold evening. She read the note again at her desk. It was only four lines long, but it had a real person in it, and a real answer.

Her mother asked how the interview went. "Awkward," Mia said. "But not bad."

She did not know it yet, but that short visit would change her whole year.
translation_zh:
米娅是校报最新来的小记者，第一项任务就让她焦虑。她要去采访社区花园里的老园丁贝尔先生。打开笔记本时，她的手在发抖。

「你的菜地怎么是死的？」她问。

这个问题很粗鲁，她一问出口就明白了。贝尔先生沉默了。两人之间的沉默很尴尬，她的脸红了。那是她这一周最难堪的一分钟。

但贝尔先生只是笑了笑。「因为我把所有东西都拔掉了，」他说，「我很好奇接下来会长出什么。」

米娅写了一条简短的笔记，道了谢，穿过寒冷的傍晚走回家。她在书桌前又读了一遍。那条笔记只有四行，但里面有真实的人，也有真实的回答。

妈妈问她采访怎么样。「挺尴尬的，」米娅说，「但不算糟。」

她还不知道，这次短短的拜访会改变她的整个一年。

vocabulary.grammar_note: 常见搭配 an awkward silence（尴尬的沉默）、feel awkward（觉得不自在）。
vocabulary.story_sentence: The silence between them was awkward, and her face turned red.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 修饰让人难堪的事；自己感到难堪要用 embarrassed。
vocabulary.story_sentence: It was the most embarrassing minute of her week.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 常用 be rude to somebody（对某人无礼）。
vocabulary.story_sentence: The question was rude, and she knew it at once.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 常用 be anxious about something（为某事焦虑）。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Mia was the newest writer on the school paper, and her first assignment made her anxious.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 常用 be curious about something（对某事好奇）。
vocabulary.story_sentence: I am curious about what will grow next.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 既可指时间短暂，也可指文字简短；名词 brief 指“简报、摘要”。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Mia wrote a brief note, thanked him, and walked home through the cold evening.

title: A Surprise for Mum and Dad
story_text: Ben wanted to cook a special dinner for his parents. Every Saturday he was on duty in the kitchen, so he already knew the work. On the big day he got up at six a.m. and started. He put cheese and tomatoes into a big pot. When the food was cooking, he ate a small snack because he was hungry. At seven a.m. his parents came home. They saw the table, the food and the candles. It looked like a small carnival in the kitchen. His mother laughed and said, "This is the best dinner of the year."
translation_zh: 本想为爸爸妈妈做一顿特别的晚餐。每个周六他都在厨房值班，所以他已经熟悉这份活儿了。大日子那天他早上六点就起床开始动手。他把奶酪和西红柿放进一口大锅。菜在煮的时候，他吃了一小份点心，因为他饿了。上午七点，他父母回到家。他们看到了餐桌、饭菜和蜡烛。厨房里看起来就像一个小小的狂欢节。他妈妈笑着说：「这是今年最好的一顿晚餐。」
image_prompt: Cosy editorial illustration for a 4:3 card: a teenage boy cooking in a warm home kitchen before sunrise, a pot on the stove, candles and a set table behind him, his parents appearing at the door, muted warm palette, no text, no watermark.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 上午的缩写，跟在具体钟点后面；不能单独当「早上」用。
vocabulary.story_sentence: On the big day he got up at six a.m. and started.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 固定短语，作表语，表示正在值班、值勤。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Every Saturday he was on duty in the kitchen, so he already knew the work.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 不可数名词，没有复数形式。
vocabulary.story_sentence: He put cheese and tomatoes into a big pot.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 可数名词，指正餐之外的小吃、点心。
vocabulary.story_sentence: When the food was cooking, he ate a small snack because he was hungry.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 可数名词，指狂欢节、嘉年华；这里用作比喻。
vocabulary.story_sentence: It looked like a small carnival in the kitchen.

title: Anna's Small Start
story_text: Anna was outgoing and friendly. She wanted to learn English well, so she bought a small notebook and wrote down one new word every night. Her teacher said, "That is a worthwhile habit." Anna liked to quote her grandmother: "A little every day is better than a lot once." With this measure, she made progress step by step. She also helped an ongoing class project about food in different countries. She learned to measure sugar for a simple cake. In the summer, she joined a carnival in her town and talked to foreign visitors. She was afraid, but she did not stop. Now she can speak to anyone.
translation_zh: 安娜性格外向又友好。她想把英语学好，于是买了一个小本子，每晚记下一个新词。她的老师说：「这是个值得做的习惯。」安娜喜欢引用她奶奶的话：「每天一点点，胜过一次做很多。」用这个方法，她一步步取得了进步。她还帮忙做一个持续进行的课堂项目，主题是不同国家的食物。她学会了为一块简单的蛋糕量取糖的用量。那年夏天，她参加了镇上的狂欢节，还和外国游客说话。她很害怕，但她没有停下。现在她能跟任何人交谈了。

vocabulary.grammar_note: 形容词，作表语，形容人爱交际、外向。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Anna was outgoing and friendly.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 形容词，作定语，表示仍在进行中的。
vocabulary.meaning_zh: 持续存在的；仍在进行的
vocabulary.story_sentence: She also helped an ongoing class project about food in different countries.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 形容词，常作定语或表语，表示值得花时间的。
vocabulary.meaning_zh: 值得做的；值得花时间的
vocabulary.story_sentence: Her teacher said, "That is a worthwhile habit."

vocabulary.grammar_note: 及物动词，常用 quote somebody 表示引用某人的话。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Anna liked to quote her grandmother: "A little every day is better than a lot once."

vocabulary.grammar_note: 及物动词，表示测量、量取；作名词时意为措施、方法（文中 With this measure 即此义）。
vocabulary.story_sentence: She learned to measure sugar for a simple cake.

title: A New Start for Tom
story_text: Tom was not happy with his body, so he began to think about his fitness. He ate chips every day and never played sports, so he felt tired all the time. One Monday he decided to change. He started a simple diet: more vegetables and fruit, less sugar. For breakfast he ate bread with butter and honey. For dinner his mother cooked rice with mushrooms. Every evening he ran in the park for twenty minutes. After four months, Tom was slim and full of energy. His friends asked him for his secret. He smiled and said, "Just start, and do not stop."
translation_zh: 汤姆对自己的身材不满意，于是开始关注自己的健康。他每天吃炸土豆条，从不做运动，所以总是觉得很累。某个周一，他决定改变。他开始了一种简单的规定饮食：多吃蔬菜和水果，少吃糖。早餐他吃涂了黄油和蜂蜜的面包。晚餐他妈妈做蘑菇米饭。每天傍晚他在公园跑二十分钟。四个月后，汤姆变得苗条又充满活力。朋友们问他秘诀。他笑着说：「只要开始，就别停下。」
image_prompt: Bright editorial illustration for a 4:3 card: a teenage boy running in a green park at golden hour, a simple breakfast of bread with honey and butter on a table in the foreground, mushroom rice, healthy and hopeful mood, muted warm palette, no text, no watermark.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 不可数名词，指身体健康、健壮。
vocabulary.story_sentence: Tom was not happy with his body, so he began to think about his fitness.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 形容词，作表语；比较级 slimmer。
vocabulary.story_sentence: After four months, Tom was slim and full of energy.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 可数名词，指日常饮食或规定的饮食；作动词时表示节食。
vocabulary.story_sentence: He started a simple diet: more vegetables and fruit, less sugar.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 不可数名词；也可作动词，表示涂黄油。
vocabulary.story_sentence: For breakfast he ate bread with butter and honey.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 不可数名词，指蜂蜜。
vocabulary.story_sentence: For breakfast he ate bread with butter and honey.

vocabulary.grammar_note: 可数名词，这里用复数泛指。
vocabulary.story_sentence: For dinner his mother cooked rice with mushrooms.

title: The Harvest Feast
story_text: In October, Ben's village had a big carnival. There was music and dancing in the square. His uncle looked after the cattle on the farm, so there was fresh milk for everyone. Ben's family cooked for the harvest feast, and everyone helped. His mother made a roast turkey with cheese inside. His father cooked a pumpkin soup and a spicy pudding. On the table there was also bread, butter and a little wine for the grown-ups. Ben ate too much and could not move. Then his little sister said, "Let's dance!" So he danced. At the end of the night, everyone went home happy and full.
translation_zh: 十月里，本的村子举办了一场盛大的狂欢节。广场上有音乐和舞蹈。他叔叔在农场里照看牛，所以每个人都有新鲜的牛奶。本一家为丰收节的盛宴做饭，大家都来帮忙。他妈妈做了一只里面塞了奶酪的烤火鸡。他爸爸煮了南瓜汤和一份辛辣的布丁。桌上还有面包、黄油，以及给大人们准备的一点葡萄酒。本吃得太撑，动都动不了。这时他妹妹说：「我们去跳舞吧！」于是他就去跳了。那天夜里结束的时候，每个人都又开心又满足地回了家。

title: Breakfast at the Cafe
story_text: Last summer, Lily took a job in a small cafe. She worked from eight a.m. to two p.m. every day. She was a waitress, so she carried food to the tables. Her aunt said, "Never be late for duty." One morning Lily got up late and ran all the way. She was angry with herself. She put the chips and a snack on the table, then smiled at every guest. Nobody knew she was tired. At two p.m. she went home and slept. Now she is never late for duty again.
translation_zh: 去年夏天，莉莉在一家小咖啡馆找了份工作。她每天从上午八点工作到下午两点。她是女服务员，所以要把食物端到桌上。她姑姑说：「值班绝不能迟到。」一天早上莉莉起晚了，一路跑着过去。她很生自己的气。她把炸土豆条和一份小吃放到桌上，然后对每位客人都微笑。没人知道她很累。下午两点她回家睡了觉。现在她值班再也不迟到了。
